column1: # This file is the stability baseline for the filter-free-set leg. The leg
# <Table> is a filter-free entity that carries an AccountId column (i.e. a
# tenant table the global query filter does NOT scope), and flags the ones
# whose enclosing statement has no "AccountId" compare.
# WHY A CLASSIFICATION FILE RATHER THAN A PURE SHAPE GATE:
#   The shape check (does the statement name an AccountId compare) cannot
#   distinguish a by-id / by-hash / caller-scoped query (safe) from an
#   unscoped one (a real tenant leak). Reviewer M4/F4 named this: the leg
#   proves "shape, not provenance." So instead of auto-failing on shape, the
#   leg records each candidate here with the REASON it is scoped, and the
#     * a NEW candidate site appears (someone added a db.<tenant-table> query
#       with no AccountId compare) — it is unclassified, so the build goes red
#       until a human classifies it (safe-by-X or a real leak);
#     * a classified site disappears (drift — the query moved or was deleted);
#   Nothing is silently un-banned: a new unscoped query cannot land without a
# FORMAT: one line per candidate:  file:line <TAB> detail <TAB> reason
#   The file:line + detail must EXACTLY match what the scanner reports; a line
#   number shift breaks the match (the test re-derives the scanner's view).
# The `reason` is a human assertion, not a machine proof. It names the scoping
# mechanism. `needs-review` is the sentinel: a site marked needs-review fails
# the stability test until it is classified or the query is fixed.

column3: by-key: unique index (AccountId, EndpointHash, IdempotencyKeyHash) is enforced by the DB; the method carries accountId and the record is written with it. The claim read is by (endpointHash, keyHash) within the caller's resolved account.
by-id: re-reads the current user by primary key (candidate.Id == user.Id) to compare against the persisted row; the user's account is already resolved by the caller. #529 legacy-import guard.
by-id+account: break-glass recovery looks up the user by email within the recovered account; the method takes accountId and the lookup is scoped to it. #265.
by-hash: login rotates the user's refresh tokens by user id (account-unique); the token hash embeds the account.
by-hash: refresh-token rotation reads by token hash; the hash is account-scoped by construction.
by-hash: same rotation path, second read by token hash.
by-user: password change revokes the user's tokens by user id (account-unique).
by-user: revokes all active tokens for a user by user id (account-unique).
by-hash: checks a minted token's durability by hash (account-scoped).
by-id: reads the user's StepUpLogoutEpoch by user id (account-unique) to check the grant is not revoked; #338 shared-state.
by-id: records a logout by bumping the user's StepUpLogoutEpoch (account-unique).
by-id: checks revocation by the user's StepUpLogoutEpoch (account-unique).
non-tenant sweep: purges expired records across all tenants (runs under the single-leader gate #271 with no tenant resolved); scoped by expiry, not by account.
non-tenant sweep: second purge query in the same sweep; scoped by expiry.
non-tenant sweep: purges expired refresh tokens across all tenants (single-leader gate #271); scoped by expiry.
